analysis: Only 222 of 670 rows (a = 1..5, b < 1500) are additively periodic with period <= 375; 22 operations have all five rows periodic, 40 none. Row 2 of D[x^y] is the Jacobsthal block swap - an independent bitset recursion agrees with the mex table for b < 1500 and with the formula for every b < 2^15; it is an involution; neither the row nor |g(b) - b| is in the OEIS.
assumptions: rows a = 1..5 computed to b < 1500 for the first spec of each of the 134 distinct operations of EXP-C07-01; a row counts as additively periodic if a period p <= 375 holds on a checked tail of length >= max(200, 3p)
row 2 of D[x^y] recomputed to b < 2^15 by an independent bitset algorithm
counterexamples: Row 2 of D[x^y] is not additively periodic (|f(2,b) - b| = J_k unbounded, Theorem 3)
falsification: H-C07-4: a row without additive period. H-C07-5: any b < 2^15 violating the formula.

hypothesis: H-C07-4 (bold): every row of every mex operation of the family is eventually additively periodic. H-C07-5 (from inspection of EXP-C07-02): row 2 of D[x^y], g(b) = mex(G u (b XOR G)) with G = {g(b') : b' < b}, satisfies g(b) = b + J_k for J_(k+1) <= b < J_(k+1) + J_k and g(b) = b - J_k for J_(k+1) + J_k <= b < J_(k+2) (k >= 1), J the Jacobsthal numbers.
methodology: Rectangular mex tables (5 x 1500); additive_period on each row; independent recursion g(b) = least v with v not in G and v XOR b not in G (bitsets); comparison with the Jacobsthal block-swap formula; OEIS checks of the row and of |g(b) - b|.
question: Is every row b -> f(a, b) (a = 1..5) of every mex operation eventually additively periodic, f(a, b + p) = f(a, b) + s, as for Wythoff's game? What is row 2 of D[x^y]?
